result.title: Competent Autonomous Driving Through Fine Tuning Vision Language Action Models with Symbolic Traffic Rules
result.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models offer a unified approach to perception, reasoning, and control for autonomous driving, but accurate action prediction alone does not establish compliance with traffic regulations. This paper presents a rule-guided VLA framework that incorporates symbolic traffic-rule feedback into policy optimisation. The framework combines supervised fine-tuning on expert demonstrations with reinforcement learning (RL) refinement using a reward that encourages encoded-rule compliance while penalising deviations from expert actions. Selected provisions of the United Kingdom Highway Code are formalised as executable first-order logic rules using PyReason, covering speed adaptation, following distance, and road-user priority. A frozen vision-language model extracts scene predicates, which are combined with vehicle-state information to assess the projected consequences of candidate control actions. Offline evaluation on held-out data collected in the CARLA simulator compares three group-based RL methods. The results show improvements in both action prediction accuracy and encoded-rule compliance over the supervised baseline. The best-performing variant increases the overall rule pass rate from 92.9% to 97.6%, with zero observed violations of the encoded road-user-priority check in the evaluated samples. These findings support symbolic rule feedback as a means of improving VLA policy alignment with explicit traffic-rule criteria.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出规则引导的 VLA 框架，用 PyReason 将英国 Highway Code 部分条款形式化为一阶逻辑规则，并由冻结的 VLM 抽取场景谓词、预测候选控制动作的后果以计算合规奖励；在专家示范监督微调基础上用三种 group-based RL 方法进行离线精调，在 CARLA 留出数据上报告动作精度与规则通过率的提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关系，但「用可执行符号规则检验候选动作的预测后果并转为奖励」可供核查作为 latent 推理轨迹的验证式监督与贡献分配线索；其冻结 VLM 输出场景谓词的做法也可能为视觉证据筛选提供参照。
